questions.question: The ozone hole was first discovered above:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Antarctica**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The ozone hole was first discovered in **1985** by a team of scientists from the **British Antarctic Survey (BAS)**, comprising **Joseph Farman**, **Brian Gardiner**, and **Jonathan Shanklin**.
 
• Their groundbreaking research was published in the scientific journal **Nature**, showing a dramatic seasonal decline in ozone levels over the **Antarctic** continent.
 
• The discovery was based on long-term data collected at the **Halley Research Station** and the **Faraday Research Station** using **Dobson spectrophotometers**.
 
• The thinning of the ozone layer was found to be most severe during the **Southern Hemisphere spring** (September to November) due to the presence of the **Polar Vortex**.
 
• The researchers observed that total ozone values had dropped by nearly **40 percent** compared to measurements taken in the late **1950s** and **1960s**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ozone Layer and Mechanism**:

 
 
• The ozone layer (O₃) is situated in the **Stratosphere**, roughly **15 to 35 kilometers** above Earth, and absorbs harmful **Ultraviolet (UV-B)** radiation.
 
• The destruction of ozone is catalyzed by **Chlorine** and **Bromine** atoms released from **Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)** and **Halons**.
 
• In **Antarctica**, extreme cold leads to **Polar Stratospheric Clouds (PSCs)**, which provide the chemical surface for **CFCs** to convert into active chlorine that destroys ozone.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Arctic**:
 
 
• While ozone depletion also occurs in the **Arctic**, it is typically less severe because **Arctic** temperatures are warmer and the polar vortex is less stable than in **Antarctica**.
 
 
 
• **Montreal Protocol**:
 
 
• Following the discovery in **Antarctica**, the international community signed the **Montreal Protocol** in **1987** to phase out **Ozone-Depleting Substances (ODS)** globally.

questions.question: Chhath Puja is primarily dedicated to which deity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sun God (Surya)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chhath Puja** is a major Hindu festival primarily dedicated to the **Sun God (Surya)** and his sister **Chhathi Maiya** (Goddess Shashthi), thanking them for sustaining life on Earth and seeking their blessings.
 
• It is predominantly celebrated in the Indian states of **Bihar**, **Jharkhand**, and **Uttar Pradesh**, as well as in the Madhesh region of **Nepal**.
 
• The festival is unique as it is one of the few Hindu celebrations that involves the worship of a **visible deity** (Pratyaksh Devta) rather than idol worship in temples.
 
• It takes place on the sixth day (Shashthi) of the lunar month of **Kartika** in the Hindu calendar, which typically falls in **October or November**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ritual Sequence**:

 
 
• **Nahay Khay**: The first day involves cleaning the house and consuming a **Satvik** meal after a holy bath in a river.
 
• **Kharna**: On the second day, devotees observe a day-long fast, breaking it after sunset with **Kheer** (rice pudding) and chapati.
 
• **Sandhya Arghya**: The third day is marked by a rigorous **36-hour fast** without water, culminating in offering prayers to the **setting sun** at a water body.
 
• **Usha Arghya**: The final day involves offering **Arghya** to the **rising sun**, after which devotees break their fast with **Thekua** (a traditional dry sweet).
 
 
 
• **Mythological Origins**:
 
 
• Legends link the festival to the **Mahabharata**, where **Karna** (the son of Surya) performed these rituals, and **Draupadi** performed them to regain her kingdom.
 
• In the **Ramayana**, it is believed that **Lord Rama** and **Goddess Sita** offered prayers to the Sun God upon returning to Ayodhya.

questions.question: What was the role of 'Adhvarya' priests according to the Yajurveda?

options.text: They conducted yajnas and chanted mantras in low tones
They wrote scriptures on music theory

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They conducted yajnas and chanted mantras in low tones**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Adhvaryu** (or Adhvarya) was one of the four primary types of priests essential for the performance of **Vedic rituals** and sacrifices during the **Vedic Period**.
 
• According to the **Yajurveda**, which is the 'Veda of Prose Mantras' or 'Book of Rituals', the **Adhvaryu** was responsible for the physical and manual execution of the **Yajna** (sacrifice).
 
• The specific duties of the **Adhvaryu** included measuring the sacrificial ground, constructing the **Vedi** (altar), preparing the sacrificial vessels, lighting the sacred fire, and offering the **Havis** (oblation).
 
• During the ritual process, the **Adhvaryu** recited the **Yajus** (sacrificial formulas) in a specific rhythmic, low-toned chant, which is a characteristic feature that distinguished them from the high-pitched recitation of the **Hotri**.
 
• The role of the **Adhvaryu** ensured the precision of the ritual's technical steps, acting as the 'chief executive' of the sacrificial ceremony to maintain the sanctity and efficacy of the **Vedic sacrifice**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Vedic Priesthood** consisted of four main categories, each associated with one of the four Vedas:

 
 
• **Hotri**:

 
 
• Associated with the **Rigveda**.
 
• Responsible for invoking the deities and reciting the **Rig** (hymns) during the sacrifice.
 
 
 
• **Udgatri**:
 
 
• Associated with the **Samaveda**.
 
• Specialized in singing the **Saman** (melodies), often compared to the musical aspect of the rituals.
 
 
 
• **Brahman**:
 
 
• Associated with the **Atharvaveda**.
 
• Served as the silent observer and supervisor of the entire **Yajna** to ensure no mistakes were made and to provide **Prayaschitta** (expiation) if errors occurred.
 
 
 
 
 
• The **Yajurveda** itself is divided into two major versions: the **Shukla Yajurveda** (White) and the **Krishna Yajurveda** (Black), containing the collections of prayers and sacrificial formulas used by the **Adhvaryu**.

questions.question: The average distance between Earth and Moon is 384,000 km. The Moon's diameter is about 3,474 km. Calculate the angular diameter of the Moon as seen from Earth (in radians).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.009 rad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Angular diameter** (or angular size) is the angle subtended by a circular object as seen by an observer from a specific distance.
 
• For celestial objects where the distance is significantly larger than the actual diameter, we utilize the **small-angle approximation** formula: θ ≈ D / d.
 
• In this formula, **D** represents the **Moon's diameter**, which is **3,474 km**, and **d** represents the **average distance** from Earth, which is **384,000 km**.
 
• The calculation is set up as θ = 3,474 ÷ 384,000, which yields the result in **radians**.
 
• Performing the division gives θ = **0.009046875 radians**.
 
• Rounding to three decimal places, the **angular diameter** of the Moon as seen from Earth is **0.009 rad**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Small-Angle Approximation**:

 
 
• This principle is used in **astronomy** and **physics** when the angle is small enough that the angle itself (in radians) is approximately equal to its **sine** and **tangent**.
 
 
 
• **Radian Measure**:
 
 
• A **radian** is the standard unit of angular measure. To convert radians to degrees, multiply by 180/π. An angle of **0.009 rad** is roughly **0.51 degrees**.
 
 
 
• **Orbital Variations**:
 
 
• The Moon follows an **elliptical orbit**. At **perigee** (closest point), its angular diameter appears slightly larger, while at **apogee** (farthest point), it appears smaller.
 
 
 
• **Visual Appearance**:
 
 
• The **Sun** has an angular diameter also measuring about **0.5 degrees**. Because the Sun and Moon have similar angular sizes, **total solar eclipses** are possible when their paths align.

questions.question: A satellite has an orbital speed of 7.8 km/s at 300 km altitude. What happens to the satellite's orbital period if its altitude increases by 200 km?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It increases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Kepler's Third Law of Planetary Motion** (the Law of Harmonies), the square of the **orbital period** (T) of a satellite is directly proportional to the cube of its **orbital radius** (r), expressed as T² ∝ r³.
 
• The **orbital radius** (r) is defined as the distance from the center of the Earth to the satellite, which is the sum of the **Earth's radius** (R) and the satellite's **altitude** (h), mathematically shown as r = R + h.
 
• When the altitude of the satellite increases from **300 km** to **500 km** (an increase of **200 km**), the total **orbital radius** (r) also increases.
 
• The relationship for the **orbital period** is derived from the formula T = 2pi sqrt{frac{r³}{GM}} ; since the radius (r) is in the numerator, an increase in **altitude** directly results in a longer **orbital period**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Orbital Velocity and Altitude**:

 
 
• The **orbital speed** (v) of a satellite is inversely proportional to the square root of the **orbital radius**, given by v = sqrt{(GM)/(r)} .
 
• As the satellite's altitude increases, its **orbital speed** decreases; at an altitude of **300 km**, the speed is approximately **7.8 km/s**, but this speed will drop as it moves to **500 km**.
 
• A slower speed combined with a longer orbital path (greater circumference) results in a significantly higher **time period** for one complete revolution.
 
 
 
• **Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Characteristics**:
 
 
• Satellites at altitudes between 160 km and **2,000 km** are considered to be in **Low Earth Orbit**.
 
• The average **Earth radius** used in these orbital calculations is approximately **6,371 km**.
 
• The **Universal Gravitational Constant** (G) is 6.674 × 10−¹¹ Nm²/kg² and the **Mass of Earth** (M) is roughly 5.97 × 10²⁴ kg.

questions.question: The GSLV Mk III (LVM3) has a payload capacity of 4000 kg to GTO. If it launches a 3600 kg satellite, and efficiency is 90%, what is the actual energy used compared to ideal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1.1 times**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The concept of **efficiency** (η) in propulsion and mechanical systems defines the ratio of the **useful energy output** (ideal energy) to the **total energy input** (actual energy).
 
• The mathematical relationship is expressed as **η = Ideal Energy ÷ Actual Energy**. To find the actual energy used relative to the ideal energy, the formula is rearranged as **Actual Energy = Ideal Energy ÷ η**.
 
• The problem specifies an efficiency of **90%**, which corresponds to a decimal value of **0.9**.
 
• To determine the factor of actual energy used, we calculate the ratio **1 ÷ 0.9**, which equals approximately **1.111...**. Hence, the actual energy used is **1.1 times** the ideal energy when rounded to one decimal place.
 
• The **payload capacity** of **4000 kg** and the specific satellite mass of **3600 kg** indicate that the rocket is operating within its structural limits, but the energy ratio remains dependent on the **system efficiency**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **GSLV Mk III (LVM3)**:

 
 
• Commonly known as the **Launch Vehicle Mark 3 (LVM3)**, it is the most powerful rocket developed by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**.
 
• It is designed to deliver heavy communication satellites into **Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO)** using a complex **cryogenic upper stage (C25)**.
 
• The vehicle utilizes two **S200 solid strap-on boosters** and an **L110 liquid-propellant core stage** to achieve the necessary thrust-to-weight ratio for heavy lifting.
 
• The **specific impulse (Isp)** and **combustion efficiency** of its engines determine the overall propellant mass required to reach a specific orbital velocity, where lower efficiency necessitates a higher **mass fraction** of fuel.

questions.question: The first-ever Indian Premier League (IPL) final in 2008 was held at which stadium?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**DY Patil Stadium, Navi Mumbai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The inaugural final of the **Indian Premier League (IPL)** took place on **June 1, 2008**, at the **DY Patil Stadium** in **Navi Mumbai**, Maharashtra.
 
• The stadium, located in the **Nerul** area, was selected as the neutral venue for the historic first final, offering a then-modern capacity of approximately **55,000** spectators.
 
• The final match featured the **Rajasthan Royals**, led by the legendary Australian spinner **Shane Warne**, against the **Chennai Super Kings**, captained by **MS Dhoni**.
 
• The match ended in a thrilling finish where the **Rajasthan Royals** chased down a target of **164** runs, winning by **3 wickets** on the final delivery of the innings.
 
• This victory established the **Rajasthan Royals** as the first-ever champions of the **IPL**, a tournament that would eventually become the world's premier domestic T20 cricket league.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **IPL 2008 Awards and Statistics**:

 
 
• **Yusuf Pathan** was named the **Player of the Match** in the final for his vital contribution of 56 runs and 3 wickets.
 
• **Shane Watson**, also from Rajasthan Royals, was declared the **Player of the Tournament** for his consistent all-round brilliance.
 
• The first **Orange Cap** was won by **Shaun Marsh** (Kings XI Punjab) for scoring 616 runs, and the first **Purple Cap** went to **Sohail Tanvir** (Rajasthan Royals) for 22 wickets.
 
 
 
• **Context of Other Stadiums**:
 
 
• **M. Chinnaswamy Stadium**: Located in **Bengaluru**, it hosted the **first-ever match** of the IPL between RCB and KKR on April 18, 2008.
 
• **Eden Gardens**: Based in **Kolkata**, it is the home ground of the **Kolkata Knight Riders** and one of the most iconic cricketing venues globally.
 
• **Wankhede Stadium**: Situated in **Mumbai**, it serves as the home ground for **Mumbai Indians** and hosted the second semi-final of the 2008 season.

questions.question: Who was India's captain of the hockey team when it won gold in the 1980 Olympics?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vasudevan Baskaran**__.

• **Vasudevan Baskaran** was the distinguished **captain** of the Indian men's field hockey team that clinched the **gold medal** at the **1980 Summer Olympics** held in **Moscow**, Soviet Union.
 
• This victory marked India's **eighth Olympic gold medal** in field hockey, a record that remains the highest for any nation in the history of the sport at the Olympics.
 
• In the high-stakes final match, the Indian team defeated **Spain** with a narrow **4−3** scoreline to stand atop the podium.
 
• Baskaran, who played the pivotal role of a **halfback**, was instrumental in leading a relatively young team to success after the disappointment of the 1976 Montreal Games.

• He was a legendary **center-half** who famously captained the Indian team to its first and only **Hockey World Cup** title in **1975** at Kuala Lumpur.

questions.question: Nitrogen is inert in the atmosphere because:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It does not react easily.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Nitrogen exists as a **diatomic molecule** (N₂) and is characterized by its high chemical stability and lack of reactivity under standard atmospheric conditions.
 
• The primary reason for its inertness is the presence of a very strong **triple covalent bond** between the two nitrogen atoms, which requires a significant amount of energy to break.
 
• The **bond dissociation energy** of the nitrogen-nitrogen triple bond is approximately **941.4 kJ/mol**, which is considerably higher than the bond energies of oxygen or hydrogen.
 
• Because of this extreme bond strength, nitrogen does not readily participate in chemical reactions at room temperature, acting as a **diluent** that slows down the combustion process of oxygen in the atmosphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atmospheric Composition**:

 
 
• Nitrogen is the most abundant gas in the Earth's atmosphere, comprising roughly **78%** of the total volume.
 
• Despite being **inert**, it is a vital component of **amino acids**, **proteins**, and **DNA** in all living organisms.
 
 
 
• **Nitrogen Fixation**:
 
 
• The strong triple bond can only be broken by high-energy processes such as **lightning strikes** or through **biological nitrogen fixation** by specific bacteria like **Rhizobium**.
 
• Industrially, the **Haber-Bosch process** uses high pressure and temperature with a catalyst to overcome this inertness to produce ammonia.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Applications**:
 
 
• Nitrogen is used to provide an **inert atmosphere** in food packaging to prevent **oxidation** and spoilage.
 
• It is utilized in **cryogenics** as liquid nitrogen for the preservation of biological samples due to its low boiling point of **−195.8°C**.

questions.question: Who was honored with a SKOCH Award for the Maharashtra Samruddhi Mahamarg project in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **SKOCH Award** was conferred upon the **Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC)** in **2025** in recognition of its excellence in infrastructure development and project management.
 
• The specific project honored is the **Maharashtra Samruddhi Mahamarg**, also known as the **Hindu Hrudaysamrat Balasaheb Thackeray Maharashtra Samruddhi Mahamarg**, which is a flagship **greenfield expressway**.
 
• **MSRDC** was recognized for successfully executing one of India’s longest access-controlled expressways, spanning **701 kilometers** and connecting the cities of **Nagpur** and **Mumbai**.
 
• The project was lauded by the **SKOCH Group** for its impact on **regional connectivity**, economic stimulation across **10 districts**, and the implementation of state-of-the-art **Intelligent Highway Management Systems**.
 
• The award highlights the corporation’s commitment to **fast-track construction**, having completed major stretches in record time while adhering to global standards of safety and sustainability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maharashtra Samruddhi Mahamarg**:

 
 
• This expressway is designed for a top speed of **150 km/h**, effectively reducing the travel time between Nagpur and Mumbai from **16 hours to approximately 8 hours**.
 
• It features over **50 flyovers**, **24 interchanges**, and specialized **wildlife overpasses**, ensuring that the ecological balance is maintained alongside industrial progress.
 
• The project facilitates the creation of **Krushi Samruddhi Nagars** (New Towns) to promote local employment and value addition to agricultural produce.
 
 
 
• **Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC)**:
 
 
• Established by the **Government of Maharashtra** in **1996**, it is a premier body responsible for the development of high-speed corridors and sea links.
 
• Notable previous projects include the **Mumbai-Pune Expressway**, which was India’s first access-controlled toll road, and the iconic **Bandra-Worli Sea Link**.

questions.question: What was India's response operation for the Myanmar earthquake in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Operation Brahma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Operation Brahma** was initiated by the **Government of India** as a rapid Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (**HADR**) mission to support neighboring **Myanmar** after a severe **earthquake**.
 
• Under this operation, India mobilized critical relief supplies, including **essential medicines**, dry rations, temporary shelters, and specialized search-and-rescue tools.
 
• The operation was executed through coordinated efforts involving the **Indian Air Force (IAF)** and the **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)** to ensure timely logistics and rescue support.
 
• This mission reflects India's proactive role as a **first responder** in the region and aligns with its strategic **'Neighborhood First' policy** of assisting neighboring nations during natural crises.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Operation Samudra Setu**:

 
 
• Launched by the **Indian Navy** in **May 2020** as part of the national effort to repatriate Indian citizens stranded overseas during the **COVID-19 pandemic**.
 
• Naval vessels such as **INS Jalashwa** and **INS Shardul** were deployed to evacuate thousands of citizens back to India.
 
 
 
• **Operation Maitri**:
 
 
• A major joint relief and rescue operation conducted by the **Indian Armed Forces** following the catastrophic **Nepal earthquake** in **April 2015**.
 
• It stands as one of India's largest emergency bilateral rescue operations, offering medical aid, engineering assistance, and food supplies.
 
 
 
• **Operation Sahayata**:
 
 
• Launched by the **Indian Navy** in **2019** to provide immediate relief to **Mozambique** following the devastation caused by **Cyclone Idai**.
 
• Indian naval ships provided medical care, clean drinking water, and helicopter-based rescue operations in affected areas.

The correct answer is __**To promote self-reliance across all sectors**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan**, which translates to **Self-Reliant India**, was launched by Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** in **May 2020**.
 
• The initiative was introduced as a strategic response to the economic disruptions caused by the **COVID-19 pandemic**, aiming to revive the national economy through structural reforms.
 
• The central goal is to make India **self-sufficient** by reducing its dependence on foreign imports and enhancing the capacities of **domestic industries** and **local manufacturing**.
 
• The government announced a comprehensive economic package worth **20 lakh crore rupees**, equivalent to nearly **10% of India's GDP**, to support this mission.
 
• The mission is built on **five essential pillars**: **Economy** (aiming for quantum leaps), **Infrastructure** (representing modern India), **System** (driven by 21st-century technology), **Vibrant Demography** (utilizing human capital), and **Demand** (harnessing the power of the supply chain).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vocal for Local**: A key component of the campaign that encourages citizens to promote and use **indigenous products** to help them achieve global standards and scale.
 
• **MSME Sector Reforms**: Under this initiative, the definition of **Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises** was revised, and **collateral-free automatic loans** were provided to boost local productivity.
 
• **Sector-Specific Focus**: The abhiyan covers various sectors including **Agriculture**, **Defense production**, **Civil Aviation**, **Power distribution**, and **Space research** to ensure comprehensive national development.
 
• **Global Integration**: While the focus is on **self-reliance**, it does not advocate for isolationism; instead, it seeks to integrate India more deeply into **global supply chains** as a reliable manufacturing hub.

questions.question: Which river forms the Dhuandhar waterfall?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Narmada**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Dhuandhar Falls** is a spectacular waterfall located in the **Bhedaghat** area of the **Jabalpur** district in **Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• It is formed by the **Narmada River**, which is the **fifth-longest river** in the Indian subcontinent and is often referred to as the **Lifeline of Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat**.
 
• The name **Dhuandhar** is derived from two Hindi words: **Dhuan** (smoke) and **Dhar** (flow), describing the smoke-like mist created by the water falling from a height of approximately **30 meters**.
 
• The river carves through the world-famous **Marble Rocks** before plunging down, creating a narrow canyon and a powerful cascade.
 
• The **Narmada River** flows through a **rift valley** between the **Vindhya** and **Satpura** ranges, moving in a westward direction towards the **Arabian Sea**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tapti River**

 
 
• It originates in the **Multai** reserve forest of **Betul** district, **Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• Like the Narmada, it is a **west-flowing river** that drains into the **Gulf of Khambhat**.
 
 
 
• **Kaveri River**
 
 
• Rising in the **Brahmagiri Hills** of the **Western Ghats** in **Karnataka**, it is a major east-flowing river.
 
• It forms the famous **Shivanasamudra Falls**, which is utilized for one of India's first **hydroelectric power** stations.
 
 
 
• **Godavari River**
 
 
• It is the **longest river** of Peninsular India, originating at **Trimbakeshwar** near **Nashik**, **Maharashtra**.
 
• Often called the **Dakshin Ganga**, it flows across the Deccan Plateau and empties into the **Bay of Bengal**.

questions.question: What is the allocated budget corpus for the Maritime Development Fund in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹25,000 crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the presentation of the **Union Budget 2025-26**, the Finance Minister announced the establishment of a dedicated **Maritime Development Fund (MDF)** with an allocated corpus of **₹25,000 crore**.
 
• The primary objective of this fund is to provide **low-cost** and **long-term financing** to the Indian maritime sector, which has traditionally faced challenges in accessing affordable credit for high-capital assets.
 
• The fund is specifically designed to incentivize **indigenous shipbuilding**, **ship repair**, and the modernization of the domestic fleet to enhance India's self-reliance in the shipping industry.
 
• By providing competitive credit, the government aims to increase the share of **Indian-flagged vessels** in global trade, thereby reducing the massive **foreign exchange outflow** currently paid as freight to international shipping lines.
 
• The **₹25,000 crore** allocation is a strategic move to support the **Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047**, which targets making India one of the top five global shipbuilding nations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047**:

 
 
• This initiative by the **Ministry of Ports, Shipping, and Waterways** aims to quadruple port capacity and promote **green shipping** over the next two decades.
 
• It focuses on the development of **Major Ports** into world-class smart ports using **AI and IoT** technologies.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Impact**:
 
 
• The **Maritime Development Fund** is expected to complement the **Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Policy (SBFAP)**, providing a holistic ecosystem for the maritime manufacturing sector.
 
• It addresses the **Blue Economy** goals by fostering sustainable growth in coastal shipping and **Inland Waterways** transport.
 
• The fund will also play a key role in the **decarbonization** of the shipping sector by supporting the construction of vessels powered by **green hydrogen** and **ammonia**.

questions.question: Which Mughal ruler consolidated the empire and is known for administrative reforms and religious tolerance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Akbar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Akbar** (reigned **1556−1605**) is recognized as the actual architect of the **Mughal Empire**, having successfully integrated various regional powers into a centralized administrative system.
 
• He introduced the **Mansabdari System**, which was a hierarchical administrative framework that determined the rank (**Zat**) and military obligations (**Sawar**) of the nobility and army officers.
 
• His land revenue policy, known as the **Zabt System** or **Dahshala System**, was developed by **Raja Todar Mal** and utilized detailed statistical data of crops and prices over a ten-year period.
 
• He is celebrated for his **religious tolerance** and the philosophy of **Sulh-i-kul** (universal peace), which aimed to treat all citizens equally regardless of their faith.
 
• In **1564**, he abolished the **Jizya** tax, a discriminatory poll tax previously levied on non-Muslim subjects, and established the **Ibadat Khana** (House of Worship) in **1575** to facilitate interfaith dialogue.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Humayun**:

 
 
• The second Mughal emperor and father of Akbar, he faced significant instability and lost the empire to **Sher Shah Suri** of the **Suri Dynasty**.
 
• He spent many years in exile in **Persia** before successfully reclaiming the throne in **1555** shortly before his accidental death.
 
 
 
• **Jahangir**:
 
 
• The son of Akbar, he is best known for his interest in **Mughal art** and **naturalism**, and for establishing the **Zanjir-i-Adl** (Chain of Justice) for direct appeals from his subjects.
 
 
 
• **Aurangzeb**:
 
 
• A grandson of Jahangir, he expanded the empire to its maximum territorial extent but is often contrasted with Akbar due to his **orthodox policies** and the reintroduction of the **Jizya tax** in **1679**.

questions.question: A rectangular loop carrying current is suspended freely in a magnetic field. What position will it naturally attain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Perpendicular to field lines**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **rectangular loop** carrying a current behaves as a **magnetic dipole**. It possesses a **magnetic dipole moment** (m), which is a vector quantity defined by the product of the **current** (I) and the **area** (A) of the loop (m = I × A).
 
• The direction of the **magnetic moment** is always **perpendicular** to the plane of the loop, as determined by the **right-hand thumb rule**.
 
• When suspended in a **magnetic field** (B), the loop experiences a **torque** (τ) that tends to rotate it. This torque is expressed by the formula: **Torque = m × B sin(θ)**, where **θ** is the angle between the magnetic moment and the field lines.
 
• A system is in **stable equilibrium** when its **potential energy** (U) is at a minimum. The potential energy for a magnetic dipole is given by **U = −mB cos(θ)**.
 
• Minimum potential energy occurs when **cos(θ) = 1**, which means **θ = 0°**. In this state, the **magnetic moment** vector is **parallel** to the external **magnetic field lines**.
 
• Since the magnetic moment vector is **perpendicular** to the **plane of the loop**, for the moment to align parallel to the field lines, the plane of the loop must naturally settle into a position **perpendicular to the field lines**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parallel to field lines**:

 
 
• In this orientation, the **plane of the loop** is parallel to the field lines, meaning the **magnetic moment** is perpendicular to the field (θ = 90°).
 
• At this position, the **torque** is **maximum** (Torque = m × B), causing the loop to rotate away from this state immediately.
 
• This configuration is utilized in **moving coil galvanometers** with **radial magnetic fields** to ensure constant maximum sensitivity, but it is not the natural resting position in a uniform field.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic Flux**:
 
 
• The loop naturally attains a position that maximizes the **magnetic flux** passing through it.
 
• **Magnetic Flux (Φ) = BA cos(θ)** is maximized when the plane is perpendicular to the field lines (θ = 0° for the area vector).
